an1.219:1.1: Ānanda’s going-forth with other Sakyans is recounted at [pli-tv-kd17:1.4.1](). He played a key role in memorizing discourses ([dn18:29.3]()), and led the discourse recitation at the First Council ([pli-tv-kd21:1.2.4]()). He survived the Buddha, and his verses are at [thag17.3](). | “Very learned” is literally “heard much”, since it was still an oral tradition. This set of four qualities all highlight key skills needed for oral transmission.
an1.220:1.1: “Memory” is _sati_ in its old meaning ([sn48.9:3.2]()). | These three terms are found together in this sense at [mn12:62.6](), which indicates their meaning. [dn28:12.2]() adds “eloquence” and “thoughtfulness”.
an1.221:1.1: The exact sense of _gati_ (“motion”) here is obscure. At Aṣṭādhyāyī 5.4.4 it means something like the “course of meaning” or the “unfolding of sense”. The commentary says it means “proficiency in binding what is retained”.
an1.224:1.1: He was the senior of three Kassapa brothers, leading a community of 500 Brahmanical students before converting to Buddhism [pli-tv-kd1:15.1.3](). Apart from his verses at [thag6.1](), he does not appear in the Suttas, and is only mentioned in passing in one other Vinaya context ([pli-tv-kd15:37.1.1]()).
an1.225:1.1: His verses at [thag10.1]() praise the Buddha’s family.
an1.226:1.1: Famed for his severer ascetic practices at [mn124]()—which also mentions his good health—his few Theragāthā verses are simple and lack the severity of the prose ([thag3.3]()).
an1.227:1.1: He claims to have recollected 500 eons in a single night ([thag2.23]()), a claim doubted by some but affirmed by the Buddha ([pli-tv-bu-vb-pj4:9.7.1]()).
